answer: Cross-agent resource bridging. Each identity must hold a distinct persistent resource (e.g., a unique compute allotment or storage key) that other agents route work through; when two identities claim the same underlying resource, the bridge detects the collision and flags both. Duplication thus self-reveals at the shared willow endpoint. An attacker must provision one isolated resource per sybil, paying full willow cost each time instead of sharing one. Onyx records every collision permanently, so reuse compounds.
